title: Monocular depth models (one image)
description: 38 depth models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.
html:
38 depth models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: one RGB image. Output: a depth or inverse-depth map. kind (a card field, result.kind) says what the numbers mean: metric = metres; scale_invariant, affine_invariant and affine_invariant_inverse are relative (unknown scale or shift, not metres). Metric models that use the focal length take model(image, intrinsics=K) (K [3, 3], pixels of the input): metric3d-vit-large and da3metric-large need it for correct metres (da3metric-large: metres = output x focal / 300; without intrinsics= a 300 px focal length is assumed, wrong for a real camera). unidepth-v2-vitl14, unik3d-vitl, depth-pro and MoGe estimate the camera themselves (given intrinsics= replace fx); zoedepth-nk and the relative models (da3mono-large too) take none. Normals-only models (kind none) return result.normals [B, H, W, 3] (unit vectors, camera frame: x right, y down, z forward).

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW measures yours. The summary uses one input, 994x1482: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under torch.compile and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable (export; memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured. The accuracy column is lower-is-better (NYUv2 AbsRel (scale+shift aligned)).

Other devices: Apple M1 Pro 16 GB, NVIDIA L4, NVIDIA L40S, NVIDIA A10, NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000; across devices.
